life_summary: Jedediah Morgan Grant was born February 21, 1816, in Windsor, New York, to a family of moderate means. In his youth, he received practical education in farming and trade skills common to rural northeastern communities. Grant converted to Mormonism in the 1830s and relocated to Ohio, then Missouri with the church. He became a forceful personality in the growing Mormon communities, gaining reputation as a stirring public speaker and community organizer. Before his death, Grant was regarded as a rising church leader with influence over younger members and significant respect for his dynamic personality and rhetorical abilities.
church_summary: Grant served early missions to the eastern United States, including Maryland, North Carolina, Virginia, and New Jersey, where he directed missionary work and gained converts. Called as a counselor to Brigham Young, Grant became a principal leader of Utah Territory in its early years. In 1856, he launched the Mormon Reformation, a movement calling members to rebaptism and renewed religious commitment through intense preaching. Known as 'Brigham's Sledgehammer' for his forceful oratory, Grant delivered fiery sermons emphasizing repentance and covenant renewal. He died unexpectedly in December 1856 from pneumonia, cutting short a promising ecclesiastical career.
